$doc: The floating bar's appearance, as data — the source of the `@component nav` block in css/components.css and of dist/react/nav.tsx. IT IS THE LARGEST BLOCK IN THE FILE TO JOIN THE FORMAT, and it forced more constructs than any other: a declaration whose value the stylesheet writes across lines (`.bar`'s two shadows), a selector list written one per line, a rule with TWO comments above it, a paragraph break inside a rule, an attribute suffix that carries a VALUE, an `@keyframes`, a comment above an override, and — three times over — a rule that exists only inside a media query and has no unconditional counterpart to override. Every one of those is a fact about the stylesheet's text or a closed widening of a vocabulary that was already closed; none of them widens what a selector may say. See components/definition.schema.json for the block that forced each, and design-system/PATTERNS.md for the method. THE BAR'S ARITHMETIC IS IN ITS COMMENTS AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING: five reveal points, each derived from the bar's measured width against the well beneath it, and four of them are `$conditions` entries named for the number they carry. Nothing here was rounded to a friendlier breakpoint on the way in.

note: Centred by opposing insets + auto margins, NOT by translateX(-50%). The
old transform made the bar the containing block for every `fixed`
descendant, and the theme puck inside it needs `position: fixed` to reach
the viewport's bottom corner on narrow screens. Same geometry, no side
effects: left/right pin the available span, `width: max-content` keeps
the bar shrink-wrapped, the margins split the difference.

declarations.aside: an object lying on the sheet

rules.name: id
note: EVERY SEAM IS OWNED BY THE SEGMENT ON ITS RIGHT — one 1px inset line on the
LEFT edge of everything except `.bar__id`, which is always first. The bar
used to be drawn the other way round (each segment carried its own right
edge) and that is a rule which cannot survive a hidden neighbour: whichever
segment happens to end the row leaves a stray line hanging off the end, so
`.bar__nav a:last-child` needed a `box-shadow: none` inside the media query
that hid `.bar__status` — the divider was coupled to a breakpoint. It was
also wrong wherever no status exists at all: cv, mcp and evals put a nav
link straight against the toggle, and the link's right edge plus the
toggle's left edge drew a 2px line on every one of those pages at every
width above 980px (two of them on cv). Left-owned edges are invariant under
hiding: the first VISIBLE segment never draws one, and no segment can end
the row with a line, whatever the breakpoints do.
The bar is `width: max-content` under a `max-width`, so when its segments
do not fit, the box stops growing and the segments simply spill out of the
right-hand end — taking the theme toggle off-screen with them. This is the
rule that decides WHICH segment gives way: `min-width: 0` lets the
identity shrink below its own text, so the name is clipped before a
control is lost. It never binds while the bar fits.

rules.name: menu
note: ---- THE NAV'S MOBILE FORM ----
Below 700px the row of anchors gives way to ONE segment that summons the
full-screen menu (see the menu component). The breakpoint is the same one
that sends the theme puck to the viewport corner, so "mobile chrome" is a
single state rather than two half-states arriving at different widths — and
it retires cv's old 560px rule, which HID that page's links with nothing in
their place.
A word, not a hamburger, by the owner's decision: this bar is made of words,
and an icon would be the only picture in it besides the assistant's face.
Styled as a nav link (it IS the navigation, folded), not as an action —
the accent block stays unique. `aria-expanded` gets the pressed ink for the
same reason `.bar__action`'s does: the announcement and the lit state must
be one fact.

rules.name: menu-open
rules.$doc: Hover and the announced open state are ONE appearance, so they are one rule under two selectors — and the stylesheet writes the two selectors on two lines, which `wrap` records. `[aria-expanded="true"]` is the first suffix in the vocabulary to carry a value; the closed form admits a quoted value and no operator, because `[aria-expanded*="tru"]` is a selector nobody enumerated.

note: ---- BELOW 700px THE INSTRUMENT DOCKS ----
The floating pill was a desktop idea that mobile shrank: folding the links
into Menu left a 203.7px object covering 54% of a 375px viewport, with an
85.6px open gap either side and content scrolling visibly beneath both.
Docked, the bar spans edge to edge, nothing slides under its sides, and the
offset drop shadow gives way to a plain hairline underline — an object
flush with three edges is not "lying on" anything, so it stops pretending.
THE ROW IS: identity (growing), the page's non-chat action if it has one
(cv's Print), and Menu at the very right — the owner's order. The chat
action leaves the bar entirely on this side of the breakpoint: chat is
expected at the bottom corner on a phone, so Ask becomes the ask-fab
component there, and `[data-ask]` is the marker that says which action
goes. The theme satellite goes too — its mobile home is the menu sheet
(see the menu component), because the corner now belongs to the chat.
One step up the type ramp for the identity, mobile only — at --text-xs it
was the smallest text on the screen anchoring its widest element (the
owner picked this from the study's frame F). Desktop keeps --text-xs, so
every measured width in the nav spec's table stays true. The menu sheet's
title takes the same step: its head is a replica of this bar, and the two
heights must not drift apart.

rules.name: ask
rules.$doc: QUERY-ONLY, AND IT POINTS FORWARDS. `.bar__action[data-ask]` has no unconditional rule for an override to name — the chat action is only ever hidden, and only here — and `.bar__action` itself is described forty rules further down, because this paragraph is about a breakpoint and the stylesheet keeps it whole. Both are the two things this rule forced: a rule declared inside a query, and a reference made from inside one.

rules.name: theme-satellite
rules.$doc: The theme puck, hidden while the bar is docked — a rule this component owns about an element it does not, exactly as `.sec--tint .well` is. It is scoped to `.bar` on purpose: the menu sheet renders the same control inside `.menu__body`, and that second rendering has to survive this. Query-only for the same reason the one above is: the satellite has no other rule in this block.

rules.name: clock
note: The clock is the one thing in the bar that moves on its own and the least
informative token in it — the hour in Sofia is a nicety, the availability is
the message. It is also 55.9px of a 319.6px segment, so it is the first
thing to give up when the bar starts crowding the page. `display: none`
rather than removal from the markup: `#local-time` has to stay in the
document or js/main.js's 30s Intl.DateTimeFormat interval writes to nothing
and starts throwing. Hiding is presentation; the words are unchanged.

rules.name: action
note: An action segment — same cell as a nav link, but it does something to the
page rather than navigating. Styled identically on purpose: the bar is one
instrument, and a button that announced itself would break the row.
---- THE BAR HAS A HIERARCHY, AND IT IS STATED ----
Left to right, every page, no exceptions:
identity → navigation → context → PRIMARY ACTION → utility
The primary action is the one thing a page most wants pressed: `Ask my Bot`
on the portfolio, `Print / PDF` on the CV. The utility — the theme toggle —
is always last, because it is the least of them and a reader looking for it
should always look in the same place.
THIS IS A CORRECTION, and the defect was the same on both pages. The primary
action was `--chrome-label-strong` on no ground: character-for-character the
colour and hover of `.bar__nav a`. So the site's most distinctive feature
read as a fourth navigation link, and on the CV the print control — the
whole reason a CV page has a bar — sat AFTER the theme toggle, so the
utility outranked the action.
It is a solid segment now. That is the same idea `.btn--solid` encodes and
the same rule `scripts/check-css.mjs` enforces for buttons: one primary
action per view, wearing the primary ink.
rules.$doc: TWO COMMENTS ABOVE ONE RULE, which is the second form of `note`. The first describes this segment; the second states the bar's whole left-to-right hierarchy, which is about the row rather than about the cell. Merging them would be a rewrite, and the stylesheet keeps them apart.

note: THE ACCENT, NOT THE INK. A solid ink segment carried the right hierarchy
and the wrong weight — at this size a near-black block reads as a hole
punched in the bar rather than as the thing to press. Blue is the site's
one brand colour and it earns its keep here: it separates the action from
the ink-coloured identity on the left AND from the chrome-grey navigation
between them, which no shade of grey could do at once.
Measured, both themes, so the promotion does not cost legibility:
light   label on accent   6.63:1     accent on the bar   6.60:1
dark    label on accent   5.21:1     accent on the bar   5.32:1
Hover and the open state commit to the ink. Blue at rest is an invitation;
ink is what it looks like once you are in it. 16.74:1 on light.

rules.name: action-open
note: An action that opens something and leaves it open wears a distinct state for
as long as it is open. This is the segment's ONLY link to the drawer: the
bar knows a button can be expanded, it does not know what it expanded.
`aria-expanded` is the state a screen reader is already being told about, so
styling it costs no new attribute and cannot drift from the announcement —
which is what a `.is-open` class beside it would eventually do. A plain
`.bar__action` (cv's Print / PDF) never carries the attribute and is
unaffected.
It reads as PRESSED rather than as lit, which is the inversion the old rule
could not express: when the resting state was quiet, "open" could be the
solid one. Now that resting is the accent, open is the ink — the same place
hover goes, because "you are in it" is one state however you got there.

rules.name: face
note: The assistant's face, in the bar. It is the same drawing as the drawer's
portrait and it is NOT a portrait here — at 1.25rem the 408 paths collapse
to a mark, which is the point: it makes the segment recognisable as the
thing the drawer opens, without pretending to be a likeness at a size that
cannot carry one. `aria-hidden` because the label beside it already says
what it is.
A CIRCLE, which crops the drawing rather than framing it. The tile inside
the SVG is a rounded square (its corner radius is 14.2387/80 = 17.8%, read
off the first path), so a 50% radius cuts the four corners off that tile.
That is the intent: the portrait reads as an avatar here, and an avatar is
round. The face sits centred in the tile, well inside the crop.

rules.name: blink
rules.$doc: The availability dot's two-step blink. A `@keyframes` has a NAME and a set of offsets and no condition at all, which is why it is a construct rather than the unnameable at-rule PATTERNS.md took it for — and why the name is checked against an `animation` in this same definition, since a keyframes name is global and nothing else could make it this component's.

note: WHEN THE STATUS IS ALLOWED IN, and why it is not 980px — or 1080px — any
more. The bar is chrome; the `.well` beneath it is the page's content
column. Once the chrome is as wide as the content it labels, it has stopped
being an object lying on the sheet and become a header. At the original
threshold the bar appeared at its proportionally LARGEST: 808px inside an
817px well at 981px viewport — 98.9% — and shrank relative to the page from
there, so the wider the screen the better it looked and the narrowest screen
that showed the status showed the worst version of it. That was the "gets
too long" report, and 1080/1280 fixed it to a measured 84.8% worst case.
THE ASK SEGMENT SPENDS SOME OF THAT BACK. `.bar__action` measures 64.0px
with the word "Ask" in it, which pushes the status-bearing bar from 752.2px
to 816.2px. Left at 1080 that is 90.7% of a 900px well — most of the way
back to the defect. So the reveal moves out to where the arithmetic works
again, rather than the new segment being squeezed to fit an old number:
bar without status   552.5px   ≤ 1199px:  55.3% of the well at 1199
bar + status + clock 872.1px   ≥ 1280px:  81.8% at 1280, 72.7% at 1440
Worst case anywhere is 81.8%, which is BETTER than the 83.6% this bar had
before the Ask segment existed — the reveal points were re-derived rather
than inherited. The price is paid by the 1080–1199px band, which loses the
availability line. That is the right thing to lose there: the status is a
passive readout, and Ask is the only route on the page to the assistant.
Identity + links + the toggle have to fit inside `calc(100vw - 1.5rem)`, and
at the full paddings they do not on a narrow screen: on a 375px viewport the
bar's content measured 367px inside a 351px box and the toggle ran to x=379 —
roughly an eighth of the control off the right edge, silently, because a
fixed element's overflow does not extend the document. These paddings bring
the content back inside the box.
THE BOUNDARY IS 600px, NOT 480px, and that is the whole point of the rule.
Tightening only to 480px left a band immediately above it where the padding
had sprung back but the viewport had not yet grown enough to pay for it, so
`.bar__id`'s overflow guard engaged and the identity was silently truncated
on four pages at once:
index  481-511px  content 488.6 in a 457-487 box   name clipped by up to 32px
evals  481-528px  content 511.9                    clipped by up to 31px
mcp    481-504px  content 487.9                    clipped by up to  7px
cv     561-574px  content 551.8 (its nav returns
at 561 — see css/cv.css)         clipped by up to 15px
600px clears the widest of those (cv's 551.8px needs a 576px viewport) with
24px to spare. Keep the slack when editing, and note that the steps here are
the SMALL end of the space ramp precisely because this is the one place where
4px matters.
SINCE THE MOBILE MENU: everything above 600px in that history still holds,
but below 700px the links are folded into `.bar__menu`, so the row this
block tightens is now three segments (identity, Menu, action), not five.
The step is kept because the identity is the segment that gives way
(`min-width: 0` + `overflow: hidden`), and at 320px the full paddings would
still clip it; the measured figures above are the record of the bar this
rule was derived against.
THE LABEL GOES, THE FACE STAYS. `Ask my Bot` is a far wider segment than the
`Ask` it replaces, and the arithmetic below was already tight enough that a
fifth segment had to be paid for out of three neighbours' padding. So below
860px the words drop and the portrait carries the segment alone — it is a
20px mark against a solid primary ground, which is legible as a target even
where it is not legible as a face.
The accessible name does not go with it: the button keeps `aria-label`, so a
screen reader and a voice-control user still get "Ask my Bot" at every width.
A control whose name disappears with its label is the failure this avoids.

rules.name: action-label
rules.$doc: The action's words, and the third query-only rule in this block. The label has no unconditional appearance at all — it is a plain span until the viewport narrows and it folds away — so there is nothing outside the query for an override to name.

note: THE FIFTH SEGMENT IS PAID FOR HERE, one step down the ramp per neighbour.
At 375px the bar was already 95.9% full: 336.6px of content in a 351px box.
An Ask segment at the ≤600px padding is 40.0px, and 336.6 + 40.0 = 376.6 in
the same 351px box — the identity would have been silently clipped, which is
the exact failure the 600px block above exists to prevent.
Nothing is hidden to make room. Three paddings each drop one step
(`.bar__id` space-3 → space-2 horizontally, `.bar__nav a` and `.theme`
space-2 → space-1), which frees 8 + 24 + 8 = 40.0px — the segment pays for
itself almost exactly:
before  135.8 id + 175.8 links +  25.0 toggle              = 336.64px
after   127.8 id + 151.8 links +  17.0 toggle + 40.0 ask   = 336.61px
Slack at 375px is 14.39px against 14.36px before — the segment is free at
the width that matters. `.bar__id`'s VERTICAL padding deliberately stays at
space-3: it is what sets the bar's height, and dropping it would shrink the
whole instrument rather than tighten one seam. (The `.theme` figures above
are the historical record of that trade: the toggle has since left the
bar's row entirely, and its ≤480px padding rule went with it.)
320px is the one width where this is not quite free, and it is worth stating
rather than discovering. The bar has been clipping the identity there since
long before Ask existed — 336.6px of content in a 296px box, which is what
`.bar__id`'s `overflow: hidden` is for — and the overflow it absorbs is
40.6px either way. What changes is how much NAME survives it: 95.2px before,
87.2px after, one monospace character. The clip was already there; it is one
glyph deeper.
SINCE THE MOBILE MENU that arithmetic is history rather than description:
the links this step squeezed are folded into `.bar__menu` below 700px, and
a three-segment bar at these paddings fits inside even a 320px box — the
identity clip is gone, not deeper. The step stays for the slack.
